It was developed to overcome limitations of standard computer graphics software which bases perspective transformations on the eye being at the origin [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that 'Standard computer graphics software provides perspective transformations based on the eye being at the origin' and that the developed method shifts the camera eye position away from the origin to avoid floating-point errors and ordering inconsistencies. This directly supports the claim that the development was intended to overcome limitations of standard software based on the eye being at the origin.
supported

This method prevents floating-point errors in screen-z values that occur when translating vertices far from the origin in standard perspective projections, which otherwise cause ordering inconsistencies during the compositing of thousands of closely spaced triangles [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that standard perspective (eye at origin) causes floating-point errors in screen-z when vertices are far from the origin, leading to ordering inconsistencies during compositing. It further details that the proposed method involves shifting the camera eye position away from the origin to establish a new geometric basis, which prevents these errors.
supported
